evidence: "The same total by the host-count form: with N full-utilization hosts, total (provisioned) = ⌈N ÷ (ρ × 0.95)⌉ = ⌈N ÷ 0.665⌉ and working = total − 1 — here N = ⌈430/17⌉ = 26, so ⌈26 ÷ 0.665⌉ = ⌈39.10⌉ = 40 provisioned, 39 working." Two sentences later the same paragraph states the normative rule correctly: "then total provisioned = ⌈N ÷ (u × ρ)⌉ and working = total − 1." Ch 8 (PDF 183) defines the symbols: "u = 0.70 utilization target, ρ = 0.95 throughput-efficiency derating."
issue: Symbol typo in the sizing formula: '(ρ × 0.95)' should be '(u × ρ)'. As printed, ρ × 0.95 = 0.9025, which contradicts the '=' 0.665 in the same equation (0.70 × 0.95 = 0.665). A reader implementing the formula from this sentence would provision ⌈26 ÷ 0.9025⌉ = 29 hosts instead of 40 — an 11-host shortfall. The numeric chain that follows (0.665, 39.10, 40) is correct under u × ρ, so only the symbol is wrong.
fix_instruction: In the sentence on book p. 90, replace '(ρ × 0.95)' with '(u × ρ)' so it matches the normative restatement later in the same paragraph and Ch 8's symbol definitions.
